metadata.subject: Arithmetic
metadata.topic: Ratios and rates in a word problem

annotator.notes: Generated a multi-turn tutoring session where the student expresses frustration. The tutor follows the scaffolding policy and emotional support guidance.

task_context.problem_statement: А Senior Center is hosting a bingo night. $2,400 in prize money will be given away. The first winner of the night will receive a third of the money. The next ten winners will each receive a 10th of the remaining amount. How many dollars will each of the next ten winners receive?
task_context.reference_solution:
The first winner will receive 2400 / 3 = $<<2400/3=800>>800.
There will be 2400 - 800 = $<<2400-800=1600>>1600 left.
The other winners will receive 1600 / 10 = $<<1600/10=160>>160 each.
#### 160

messages.content:
I have to do this problem: А Senior Center is hosting a bingo night. $2,400 in prize money will be given away. The first winner of the night will receive a third of the money. The next ten winners will each receive a 10th of the remaining amount. How many dollars will each of the next ten winners receive?

I honestly hate word problems. I'm just not a math person and I can't even figure out where to start. Can you just tell me the answer?

I hear you—word problems can feel overwhelming because there's so much text to sift through. It's okay to feel frustrated, but I know you can handle this if we take it one small piece at a time. Instead of jumping to the end, let's just look at the first part. What happens to the prize money when the first winner is paid?
It says they get a third of the money. I guess that's 2400 divided by 3? But I always mess up the division.
You've got the right operation! Dividing by 3 is exactly how to find a third. Why not try that calculation? If you're unsure, you can break 2400 into 2100 and 300 to make it easier.
Okay, 2400 / 3 is 800. Is that right? Now what? I'm probably going to mess up the 'remaining amount' part because that's where I usually get confused.
That's exactly right! You're already making progress. To find the 'remaining amount,' just think about it as the total money minus what the first winner already took. What does that leave us with?
So 2400 minus 800... that's 1600. I feel like I'm just guessing at this point, this is so annoying.

You aren't guessing—you're calculating correctly! 1600 is the correct remaining balance. You're actually cruising through the hardest parts. Now, the problem says the next ten winners each get a 10th of that remaining amount. How would you calculate a 10th of 1600?
A 10th means divide by 10, right? So 1600 / 10 is 160. Is that the final answer for each person?
Spot on. You've followed the logic perfectly from start to finish. Each of those ten winners receives 160 dollars. Great job sticking with it even when it felt frustrating!
